title: DeepSeek-R1 Distill 7B / 8B / 14B / 32B
name: DeepSeek-R1 Distill 7B / 8B / 14B / 32B
description: DeepSeek-R1 Distill 7B / 8B / 14B / 32B is the distilled reasoning line for teams that want R1-style chain-of-thought behavior without the full 671B MoE serving footprint.

hardware.recommended_gpu: For the 32B variant, community guidance favors high-memory GPUs or multi-GPU configurations served with tensor parallelism; 7B/8B fit easily on commodity single-GPU cards.

runtime_compatibility.notes: The official release documents a vLLM serving command for the distilled models.
The official release documents an SGLang serving command for the distilled models.
The release states the distilled models can be used like Qwen or Llama models, but it does not explicitly publish a Transformers compatibility matrix.

deployment.recommended_quantization: BF16 for the 14B/32B variants when reasoning fidelity is the priority, and lower-bit quantization for 7B/8B when cost and latency dominate.

license_info.name: MIT License / Base-model Licenses
license_info.notes: The official release permits commercial use, modifications, and distillation, while noting that Qwen-derived checkpoints inherit Apache 2.0 lineage and Llama-derived checkpoints inherit Llama licenses.

best_for: Production reasoning endpoints that need much lower footprint than the full R1 model.
Cost-sensitive agent workflows where explicit reasoning is still valuable.
Local or edge-adjacent deployments for code, math, and logic tasks, especially in 7B/8B form factors.
avoid_for: Systems that require the full frontier MoE capacity of DeepSeek-R1.
Workloads that cannot tolerate long generation traces or higher token budgets from reasoning.
Ultra-low-latency chat tasks where reasoning overhead is unnecessary.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Use the 7B/8B variants for cost-efficient reasoning in small deployments, and the 14B/32B variants when you need better reasoning quality and can pay the extra memory and latency cost.
deployment_risks: Malformed reasoning traces if prompting is not configured according to the teacher model requirements.
Extra latency and token budget consumption on reasoning traces that don't terminate cleanly.
failure_modes: Failing to parse the output format correctly if the <think> tag formatting contract is breached.
High memory fragmentation during batch serving of the 32B variant under large sequence sizes.
common_mistakes: Treating these distills as plain chat checkpoints, which can reduce reasoning quality or trigger malformed reasoning traces.
Applying custom system prompts which can break the distilled reasoning alignment.
operational_notes: The official usage recommendations warn against adding a system prompt and advise placing all instructions in the user prompt, which is a deployment-critical difference from many standard chat models.
The release recommends enforcing a leading <think>\n to keep the model in reasoning mode, which directly affects routing, prompt templates, and output parsing in production.
For math tasks, the official recommendation is to request step-by-step reasoning and a boxed final answer, which improves reliability for structured reasoning workloads.

The distilled models are meant to be used like Qwen or Llama models, but the release explicitly says the local run settings and tokenizer/config should follow DeepSeek’s recommended settings rather than generic base-model defaults.

Variant differentiation (Identity): DeepSeek-R1 Distill 7B / 8B / 14B / 32B is the distilled reasoning line for teams that want R1-style chain-of-thought behavior without the full 671B MoE serving footprint.
Variant differentiation (File Formats): Safetensors format is officially published, while GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ and Apple Silicon MLX/ONNX formats are Not Published in official checkpoints.
Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): 7B/8B fit easily on commodity single-GPU cards, while 32B requires high-memory or multi-GPU environments.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): official checkpoints include Hugging Face distills for 7B, 8B, 14B, and 32B sizes.
Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): vLLM and SGLang commands are explicitly documented in official release instructions, whereas llama.cpp is undocumented.
Variant differentiation (Deployment): base-model licensing applies to distilled variants (Apache 2.0 for Qwen, Llama License for Llama-derived), separate from the repository license.
Variant differentiation (License): permissive weights allow distillation and commercial use.
Variant differentiation (Status): officially released production checkpoint targeted at robust structured reasoning.
